content:
In a two-hour interview on the PBD Podcast, Sam Shamoun told his hosts that the Quran plagiarises Paul, that Islam licenses the sexual use of housemaids, that Muhammad (peace be upon him) abandoned an elderly wife, and that nine in ten converts leave Islam within five years. He called Muhammad "an antichrist" and Islam "very polytheistic".[1]

He also told them how he prepares. This article aims to provide context to his claims, insha'Allah, in nine points, each quoted from the interview with its time and set against the sources he names. We checked his words; he, by his own account, rarely checks theirs.

Asked how many times he had read the Quran, he answered: "I don't know really. Uh maybe once or twice."[2] The Bible fared little better: "I probably read it two or three times… I don't really read it all the way through."[3]

Asked whether he studies daily, he said: "I'm not studying. I'm writing to equip people with articles so they can use it in battle."[4] He has no formal training to fall back on: he told the hosts he was thrown out of high school in his third year and has "never been to college".[5]

Strength: firm. These are his own words. A man who has read the Quran once or twice tells audiences of millions what it says, and the points below show what that costs him.

He told the hosts that the hadith "what no eye has seen, no ear has heard" is "a plagiarism of Paul", because "Muhammad took Paul's words that statement comes from 1 Corinthians 2:9".[6]

Paul does not claim the words as his own. He introduces them with "But, as it is written", and the commentators trace them to the prophet Isaiah: "no eye has seen a God besides you, who acts for those who wait for him" (Isaiah 64:4).[7]

The hadith itself is a hadith qudsi, in which the Prophet relays God's words: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived."[8] Strength: firm. On his own test, Paul plagiarised Isaiah. A shared promise of God across three scriptures is what a Muslim expects.

He set Quran 22:6–7, "Allah is the Truth" who gives life and raises the dead, beside John 5 and asked "who's plagiarizing whom", arguing that Jesus there "applied it to himself" and so "clearly Jesus claimed to be God".[9]

The same chapter answers him. "The Son can do nothing of his own accord, but only what he sees the Father doing" (John 5:19). "As the Father has life in himself, so he has granted the Son also to have life in himself" (John 5:26). "I can do nothing on my own" (John 5:30).

Life that is granted is life received. The Quran's Jesus says the same thing in his own words: "I quicken the dead, by Allah's leave" (3:49).[10] Strength: firm. He read verse 21 and stopped before the verses that qualify it.

He argued that in John 14:6 Jesus calls himself "the truth" and "the life", names that in Islam belong to God, so "he just claimed to be more than a man".[11]

A few verses later the same speaker says, "the Father is greater than I" (John 14:28). In his prayer he names "the only true God" and sets himself beside that God as the one sent: "that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent" (John 17:3).

Strength: firm. A messenger can be the way to God and bring the truth and life God gives. The Gospel of John says so in the passages he left out.

Citing Quran 78:31–33, he told the hosts that "the Quran says you'll spend all eternity deflowering them", then corrected himself in the next breath: "When I say Quran, Quran says you will have sex with them. But the hadith go graphic."[12]

The verses he cited list gardens, vines, companions of equal age and a full cup. None of them describes an act, and the detail he gave is, by his own admission, not in the Quran at all. The "young boys serving you" he mocked are the servants of 56:17, youths who bring cups and pitchers.

Strength: firm. He attributed to the Quran what he admits it does not say, and supplied the rest from his own imagination.

He said that women who go to Saudi Arabia as maids "don't know they're signing up for sex. That's part of the deal… That's in chapter 4, verse three of the Quran."[13]

The phrase in 4:3 refers to slaves. A housemaid is a free woman hired for wages, and Islamic law treats the enslavement of a free person as one of the gravest crimes: the Prophet said God himself will be the opponent, on the Day of Resurrection, of "a man who sold a free man and ate his price".[14]

Saudi Arabia abolished slavery by royal decree in 1962.[15] The abuse of domestic workers is a crime by the law of Islam and of that state. Strength: firm. He turned a crime against Islamic law into a doctrine of it.

Of Sawda bint Zam'a he said that the Prophet "was no longer attracted to her", that she was "a huge fat lady", and that "he left this woman in a house all by herself the rest of her days".[16]

The report he relies on says something else. Aisha relates that Sawda, when she had grown old, feared that the Prophet would part from her and offered her day to Aisha, and he accepted; al-Albani grades the report hasan sahih.[17] The verse revealed on it says that a settlement between husband and wife "is best" (4:128).[18]

She stayed his wife and a Mother of the Believers (33:6). Nothing in the report says she was left alone, and nothing says why except her own fear of age. Strength: firm. The insult about her body is his; the abandonment is his invention.

He told the hosts that "one statistic showed that about over 90% of converts leave Islam in 5 years", and added, "I don't know when the last statistic came out."[19]

No survey we can find reports such a figure. The Pew Research Center, which measures religious switching in the United States, found that the share of Americans who leave Islam is offset by the share who become Muslim.[20]

Strength: firm. A number he could not date, from a study he could not name, is a number he made up or repeated without checking.

He argued that if the Quran is the uncreated speech of God, Muslims are left asking "How many uncreated entities do you have? Two.", and that because the Quran "will appear as a man interceding" on the Day of Judgement, it has "its own consciousness", so Islam is "very polytheistic".[21]

Speech belongs to the speaker; it is an attribute, and the classical creed says of it that it is neither God nor other than God for exactly that reason. The hadith he means says the Quran, and the two long surahs, will come "as two clouds… or two flocks of birds" pleading for those who recited them, which is the language of image.[22]

His own Bible speaks the same way: "The voice of your brother's blood is crying to me from the ground" (Genesis 4:10). No Christian counts Abel's blood as a divine person. Strength: firm.

The bottom line

Nine claims, and nine failures: a promise he credits to Paul that Paul credits to Isaiah, chapters of John he quoted only to the verse that suited him, a Quran he quotes for what he admits is not in it, a crime he calls a doctrine, an old woman's choice he calls abandonment, and a statistic he cannot source. He told his hosts he has read the Quran "maybe once or twice", and it shows.

Late in the interview he called the record of his past "lies and slander being used to discredit me".[23] The courts of Illinois, which heard him under oath, found his testimony "not credible"; we set out what they found in Sam Shamoun under oath. Readers who meet his claims should check them as we have: against the sources. God knows best.
